category_overview: These three tools are vertical specialists anchored to a proprietary corpus or system of record rather than general assistants: CoCounsel sells agentic AI on top of Thomson Reuters' Westlaw, Practical Law and Checkpoint content; Datasite embeds AI inside the virtual data room where deal documents already sit; Optro (formerly AuditBoard) embeds agents inside the GRC system of record. They barely overlap with one another, but all three compete for budget and attention with horizontal assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Microsoft 365 Copilot, and all three answered in 2026 by shipping MCP connectors so corporate instances of those assistants can reach their governed content and workflows under existing permissions. Enterprises typically standardise on one platform per function (legal research/drafting, deal rooms, GRC) and pair it with a horizontal assistant, because switching costs are driven by the underlying content subscriptions, deal archives or control libraries rather than the AI layer. Pricing is contract-based with no transparent enterprise list price except CoCounsel's self-serve small-firm tiers, and the shared governance pattern is explicit no-training commitments, SOC 2 plus ISO attestations (CoCounsel and Datasite also hold ISO 42001), zero-retention arrangements with model providers, and citation traceability with human approval as the primary control.

tools.name: Thomson Reuters CoCounsel
tools.vendor: Thomson Reuters (Legal Professionals and Tax & Accounting segments). Product family: CoCounsel Legal, CoCounsel Essentials, CoCounsel Tax, CoCounsel Audit & Accounting. Brief's vendor guess is correct; CoCounsel originated at Casetext, acquired by TR in 2023 for $650M.
tools.what_it_is: Thomson Reuters' 'Fiduciary-Grade AI' assistant family grounded in Westlaw, Practical Law and Checkpoint content. CoCounsel Legal is a web app with a Drafting Agent in Microsoft Word, Outlook/Teams add-ins, DMS connectors and a Claude MCP connector; CoCounsel Tax and Audit & Accounting are separate Checkpoint-based web apps for tax and audit teams.
key_capabilities: Deep Research with Deep Research Verify, which checks that cited Westlaw/Practical Law authority supports each assertion
Tabular Analysis: review up to 10,000 documents against 100 questions, returned as filterable tables
Westlaw Brief Builder, matter-specific Workspaces and a Drafting Agent inside Word; the Essentials tier covers review, comparison, summarisation and knowledge search
CoCounsel Tax: Checkpoint-cited research and document analysis; the Oct 2026 next-gen version writes and runs code for calculations and builds multi-tab Excel workbooks
tools.enterprise_data_handling: All tiers (product FAQ): prompts and content are not used to train or improve CoCounsel and are not stored by OpenAI or Google; model providers are contractually barred from training and are called via zero-retention APIs; TLS 1.2 in transit, AES-256 at rest; retention is configured per organisation account; storage in the US with regional options for the UK, Australia and Canada. CoCounsel Legal: SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, FedRAMP In Process (TR blog, Feb 2026); ISO 27001 also cited (Dec 2025). All CoCounsel Tax plans list 'SOC 2 security'. No HIPAA statement found on opened pages.
tools.licensing_pricing: USD 'starting at' self-serve monthly prices on an annual contract; firms over 10 attorneys must contact sales: CoCounsel Essentials $340.85/month; Practical Law Dynamic Tool Set with CoCounsel Essentials $882.30/month; CoCounsel Legal $1,694.90/month (TR plan comparison page). Competitor Spellbook (updated 21 Oct 2026) reports a 5-attorney CoCounsel Legal quote of $2,461.60/month (~$492/user) and 12%/18% two- and three-year discounts. CoCounsel Tax Research and Audit & Accounting are contact-sales. Bundled with Westlaw Advantage/Practical Law, not with Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace.
tools.integrations: Westlaw, Practical Law, KeyCite, Checkpoint, ONESOURCE+; Microsoft Word, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint; iManage, NetDocuments, Box, HighQ, Litify, Smokeball, DeepJudge, Supio, Reveal; Claude via MCP (AWS Amazon Quick MCP forthcoming); tax: UltraTax, Engagement Manager, Guided Assurance, SharePoint knowledge base.
tools.recent_developments: Jan 2026: CoCounsel Legal launched in the UK. Feb 2026: one million users in 107 countries; proprietary Thomson LLM disclosed (now powering Tabular Analysis). May 2026: expanded Anthropic partnership; next-gen rebuilt on the Claude Agent SDK with a Claude-to-CoCounsel MCP connection. 20 Aug 2026: next-gen CoCounsel Legal GA in the US (Brief Builder, Workspaces, Drafting Agent in Word, Deep Research Verify). Oct 2026: Multinational Profile covering 100+ countries, with Australia, Brazil, Canada, Singapore and UAE rollout; 22 Oct 2026 fully agentic CoCounsel Tax, Audit & Accounting for US customers. No rename: the former Casetext brand is now TR's umbrella AI brand.
tools.best_fit_departments: 06 Legal Affairs: strongest fit, purpose-built for contract review, legal research and clause comparison. 23 Taxation: strong, but requires the separate CoCounsel Tax subscription grounded in Checkpoint. 07 Regulatory Compliance: weak-to-partial; no dedicated compliance edition appears on opened pages, so value is indirect via Practical Law/Checkpoint content and TR's regulated-industry positioning.
tools.training_notes: Specialist band, 24-40 hours: matter scoping and Workspaces hygiene; designing Tabular Analysis question sets; verifying every citation with Deep Research Verify and KeyCite; privilege, confidentiality and retention settings; supervising agentic drafts in Word rather than accepting them; tax users must reconcile generated calculations and workbooks to Checkpoint authority; knowing Essentials vs Legal vs Tax entitlements.
tools.caveats: No enterprise price list; true cost includes Westlaw/Practical Law subscriptions (Lawyerist calls it an 'add-on product'). Next-gen legal and tax features were US-only at launch with other regions phased through late 2026. Outputs still need professional verification. The FAQ names only OpenAI and Google providers while 2026 releases cite Claude, so confirm provider terms contractually. FedRAMP is only In Process; HIPAA not stated; Tax Essentials limits Checkpoint citations.

tools.name: Datasite AI
tools.vendor: Datasite (formerly Merrill DataSite), delivered through the Datasite Diligence and Acquire data rooms, Blueflame AI (acquired 2025) and Grata Intelligence. Brief's guess is correct; 'Datasite AI' is an umbrella for these capabilities, not a single SKU.
tools.what_it_is: AI embedded in Datasite's M&A virtual data rooms: native tools (Summarize, Explain This, Enhanced Review, Redaction AI, translation) plus the agentic Blueflame AI assistant inside Diligence (sell-side) and Acquire (buy-side) projects. It runs as a web app, iOS/Android apps and APIs, with an MCP server that lets corporate Claude, ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot query the data room under existing permissions.
key_capabilities: Blueflame AI assistant: semantic search, source-cited answers, Q&A response drafting, gap and risk flagging without downloading files
Enhanced Review extracts and compares terms across documents; Summarize and Explain This decode long files and clauses
Redaction AI identifies 120+ sensitive data types across the full document set; full document translation in 17+ languages
Acquire: findings and issues tracking linked to sources, AI folder building from request lists, deal dashboards; Grata Intelligence covers 20M+ companies for target sourcing
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Single enterprise platform, no tiers. Customer data is never used to train models, enforced through enterprise agreements; all AI providers run under zero-data-retention; redaction is applied permanently before AI processing; vectors are project-scoped; AI requests route through regional servers and documents stay in the room; Blueflame AI and the MCP server inherit user permissions; Project Admins switch AI on or off per Diligence/Acquire project; all AI interactions are audit-logged (June 2026). Certifications: ISO 27001 (since 2007), ISO 27017/27018/27701, ISO 42001 (Oct 2025, first VDR provider), SOC 2 Type II annually; GDPR and CPRA; Microsoft Azure hosting with encryption in transit and at rest. HIPAA and FedRAMP are not stated.
tools.licensing_pricing: No list prices: 'Datasite pricing is customized for every transaction', quoted per deal scope, requirements and timeline; a 90-day free trial is offered on Diligence. Competitor Peony (updated 17 Oct 2026) cites buyer-reported USD $0.40-$0.85 per page (~$0.60 typical), ~$68k average annual spend, a $50k+ floor per mid-market deal and surcharges for Excel, rich media, storage and extensions. Not bundled with any productivity suite.
tools.integrations: Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Rogo via the Datasite MCP server; Blueflame Snowflake MCP connector (Notion and HubSpot planned); Datasite APIs; Grata Intelligence; Sherpany board portal; Blueflame Excel add-in announced as coming.
tools.recent_developments: June 2025: acquired Grata (private-market intelligence). Jul-Aug 2025: acquired agentic-AI firm Blueflame AI, forming Datasite's Intelligence Unit. Oct 2025: ISO 42001 certification. May 2026: Blueflame AI embedded inside Diligence and Acquire data rooms. June 2026: published AI security architecture and MCP server. Oct 2026: Grata now marketed as 'Grata Intelligence' (rename); new 'Datasite Connect' AI workspace due 4 Nov 2026.
tools.best_fit_departments: 03 Corporate Development & M&A: strong fit for due diligence summaries, Q&A management and issue tracking across the deal lifecycle. Fit is weak for 'valuation assumptions' (it is not a modelling tool) and only partial for integration trackers, served indirectly via Acquire findings tracking and Archive.
tools.training_notes: Specialist band, 20-30 hours: permission and folder design; per-project AI toggles; Q&A workflow and Similar Questions de-duplication; redaction QC before AI exposure; verifying AI summaries against cited sources; governing MCP access from corporate Claude/Copilot; Grata sourcing basics; controlling per-page cost.
tools.caveats: Quote-only premium pricing with per-page surcharges. Steep learning curve, complex dashboard and frequent re-authentication prompts (independent review). AI outputs must be verified; redaction applied before AI is permanent. Blueflame-in-data-room and MCP are 2026-new; Connect is not GA until Nov 2026. HIPAA, FedRAMP and explicit data-residency regions are not stated on opened pages.

tools.name: AuditBoard AI
tools.vendor: Optro (formerly AuditBoard; founded 2014 as SOXHUB; owned by Hg since 2024). RENAME: the brief's 'AuditBoard' is outdated. The company rebranded as Optro on 9 March 2026 and its AI is marketed as 'Optro AI'; the SOX module SOXHUB became 'Controls Management'.
tools.what_it_is: Cloud GRC platform (a 'system of record and action') for internal audit, SOX, risk, infosec and compliance with embedded agents: Optro Assistant, Autonomous Testing, Agentic Compliance/TPRM and AI Governance. It is a web platform with a mobile app, 150+ integrations, REST/SCIM APIs and an MCP server for ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot.
key_capabilities: Autonomous Testing reads unstructured evidence (dense PDFs, video walkthroughs), executes attribute tests and returns cited, external-audit-ready Excel workpapers; extended from SOX to operational audit in Oct 2026
Audit planning with agent-suggested risk scores for auditable entities plus Intelligent Staffing recommendations
Drafts audit descriptions, executive summaries, issue action plans, scoping memos (Document Intelligence) and reusable Board Reporting sections
Optro Analytics full-population testing and Continuous Control Monitoring; AI Governance with shadow-AI discovery and EU AI Act/NIST AI RMF/ISO 42001 mapping
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Single enterprise platform; AI features are opt-in per customer. 'Optro does not use customer data to train Optro AI'; AI runs in customer-specific encrypted environments using Microsoft Azure OpenAI plus in-house models; every agent action is logged and 'nothing is approved, routed or completed without a person'. Attestations: SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II (2025 reports), ISO 27001 (BSI, since 2022), HIPAA Type 1 report, TX-RAMP, CSA STAR, NIST 800-53 assessed, GDPR/CCPA; hosted on AWS infrastructure meeting FedRAMP Moderate requirements (not a product authorisation); single-tenant instances, AES-256, TLS 1.2/1.3, AWS KMS, SAML 2.0, SCIM, MFA, IP allowlisting, NIST-compliant deletion. Data-residency regions are not published.
tools.licensing_pricing: No published prices ('Request Optro Pricing'); annual subscription priced per core user and per module with unlimited stakeholder licences. Third-party ERP Research (2026) reports a median of about USD $46,000/year with a $21k-$150k range; Techno-Pulse (Jul 2026) cites $30k-$75k for 5-15 auditors scaling to $150k+. Whether AI is a paid add-on is not stated. Not bundled with any suite.
tools.integrations: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Jira, ServiceNow, Workday, Google Drive, Microsoft Office; AWS, Azure and Snowflake for evidence collection; SAP, Oracle and NetSuite ERP connectors; HRIS/CRM/accounting connectors; REST and SCIM APIs; MCP server for ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot.
tools.recent_developments: Oct 2025: acquired AI-governance firm FairNow and launched 'Accelerate' AI. 9 Mar 2026: AuditBoard renamed Optro (domain optro.ai; OpsAudit, RiskOversight, CrossComply kept; SOXHUB became Controls Management). Apr 2026: MCP server. May 2026: acquired YC-backed Midship (agentic SOX automation, 'up to 87%' claim). 15 Oct 2026: GRC Intelligence Platform with domain-trained agents for audit, compliance, TPRM and AI governance; Agentic AI Governance previewing for 2027. Named Leader in Forrester Wave GRC Q2 2026.
tools.best_fit_departments: 08 Internal Audit: strong fit (OpsAudit audit management plus Autonomous Testing and Controls Management for SOX, with audit-ready workpapers). It also serves enterprise risk, compliance and infosec teams that are not in the handbook mapping for this tool.
tools.training_notes: Specialist band, 24-32 hours: tenant, RBAC and SSO setup; AI opt-in and guardrail configuration aligned to risk appetite; evidence quality and sampling vs full-population analytics; reviewing and approving agent-generated workpapers rather than accepting them; audit-log and traceability review; MCP governance; updating vendor-risk files and SAML metadata for the Optro name.
tools.caveats: The 87% SOX automation claim originates from acquired Midship and lacks independent validation. Module-based licensing invites cost creep; no on-premise option; US-centric with limited multilanguage support. The rebrand leaves stale documentation, review-site listings and certificates; confirm DPAs carry current no-training terms. FedRAMP applies to hosting, not the product; residency regions unspecified.
